- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.67) — model tends to overshoot early in the cycle.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (especially <0.33) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 75+), leading to overcorrection and overshoot in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds prices too high after peaks, especially when sentiment is flat or negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows lagged sensitivity to sentiment — if sentiment drops below 0.33, model doesn’t adjust downward quickly enough.
- When sentiment is 0.00, model often fails to recognize trend reversal and continues to forecast upward.
- Avoid extrapolating recent highs — if last 3–5 days are rising, model tends to overpredict further gains.
- If sentiment is positive but recent price action is falling, model ignores the reversal signal and continues upward bias.
